Sara (Support): FYI HelioFin reported repeated 429s hitting the API during their top-of-minute batch window. They say it spikes for ~30s each minute.
AJ (SRE): Can you paste an example response headers and a short sample of their request pattern? RPM vs TPM would be helpful.
Sara (Support): Copying what Helio sent:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 1200\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 27\nX-Request-Id: req_01Fxxxx\n\nClient says they do ~20 concurrent streams, each sending short chat completions every 2s for 30s at top-of-minute.
Devin (Infra): That pattern will align badly with minute buckets. If their clients are synced to the minute boundary, you get a concentrated RPM/TPM hit.
AJ (SRE): Can you also share a short log tail from the gateway around the incident window? We need the throttle reason (rpm/tpm/conn) and which node returned the 429.
Sara (Support): Helio attached this snippet:
```\n2024-03-18T12:59:00Z gateway-01 INFO request=req_01Fxxx status=200 path=/v1/chat
2024-03-18T12:59:31Z gateway-02 WARN request=req_01Fxxx status=429 reason=rpm_exceeded tenant=heliofin
2024-03-18T12:59:33Z gateway-01 WARN request=req_01Fyyy status=429 reason=rpm_exceeded tenant=heliofin
``` 
Mike (ProdEng): Looks like per-tenant minute-bucket exhaustion (rpm_exceeded). If they're on Dedicated, check whether we have a per-tenant smoothing policy or if edge-level shaping is kicking in.
AJ (SRE): I'll grep the rate-limiter logs for tenant=heliofin across the cluster. Assigning myself to investigate. Quick checklist:
- verify configured RPM/TPM for their plan
- check cross-AZ minute-alignment/skew
- confirm if prefix caching or streaming keeps connections open
Devin (Infra): Also check for upstream proxies doing retries. Retries + sync -> amplification. Ask Helio to disable client-side aggressive retries while we investigate.
Sara (Support): Replied to customer asking to run this curl to capture headers and timing and paste back:
```\ncurl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}]}'\n``` 
Please include the `X-RateLimit-*` headers.
AJ (SRE): Found entries in limiter logs: `tenant=heliofin window=60s limit=1200 used=1245 reset_in=15s` — burst overflow. Also saw requests concentrated at second ~0-30 each minute.
Ops Oncall: We can do a temporary quota bump for Helio to keep them healthy while we root cause. How long do we need? 1 hour? 4 hours?
Mike (ProdEng): Start with 1 hour and ask them to confirm. Meanwhile recommend client changes: add jitter to schedule, exponential backoff on 429, and reduce concurrency to 8 streams if possible.
Sara (Support): Customer agreed to the 1-hour bump and will test. They also agreed to try a client-side jitter patch this afternoon.
AJ (SRE): Follow-ups for the postmortem:
- add metric for per-tenant intra-minute variance (how concentrated requests are in the first 30s)
- evaluate smoothing/burst allowances on Dedicated vs Hosted
- ensure our edge nodes respect a shared window (fix rare minute boundary skew)
Devin (Infra): Short-term mitigation doc to share with customers:
- avoid top-of-minute cron/cron-like syncs
- implement jitter +/- 15s for periodic tasks
- prefer spreading long-lived streams vs many short reconnects
Sara (Support): Action items: AJ will apply emergency bump (ops will run change), Devin will draft customer-facing guidance, Mike will coordinate an operator runbook for quota bump reqs.
AJ (SRE): Bump applied at 2024-03-18T13:02:02Z — increased RPM for tenant=heliofin from 1200 -> 2400 for 1 hour. Ticket -> INC-8793.
Ops Oncall: Change validated, no further 429s in next 3 minutes of sampling from their agent.
Sara (Support): Customer confirmed reduced 429s after bump and will implement jitter change. Marking this as a busy support handoff -> SRE investigation.
Mike (ProdEng): We'll schedule a follow-up next week to propose a longer-term quota if their workload pattern is steady. Also check whether Dedicated contract allows for minute smoothing tweaks.
AJ (SRE): I'll post findings in a short postmortem and link to runbook. Leaving thread open until PM confirms next steps.
customer-jira-bot: New ticket HELIO-312 created for customer's request to increase baseline quota.
Sara (Support): Thanks all — keeping thread open until postmortem. :thumbsup:
